topic: Why a 256-TOPS box can honestly chart ahead of a 1000-TOPS DGX Spark: sparse TOPS, prefill, and the 273 GB/s decode tie
title: 256 TOPS vs 1,000 TOPS: reading the fine print
description: Working description; stage 05 overwrites. A 40 W box claims its 256 TOPS beats DGX Spark's 1000 TOPS on Qwen prefill; the fine print says why, and why chat speed is something else.
hook_text: DGX Spark's label isn't its speed.
hook_candidates: DGX Spark's label isn't its speed. *
A forty-watt box claims it beats NVIDIA's thousand-TOPS giant.
DGX Spark or the forty-watt challenger? Bandwidth decides.
One number ties these boxes: two hundred seventy-three gigabytes a second.
The thousand-TOPS machine is not the fast one.
Two hundred fifty-six TOPS just picked a fight with a thousand.
NVIDIA's biggest number is a footnote.
You are comparing AI boxes by the wrong number.
A forty-dollar-a-year-to-run box says it beats NVIDIA's desk giant.
Reading the label, not the benchmark, settles this box fight.
The spec sheet says four times faster. Your chat says otherwise.
narration_full: DGX Spark's label isn't its speed. NVIDIA's footnote calls its thousand theoretical, sparse math that skips zeros. You read the label's TOPS, its peak-math rating, and assumed four times meant four times faster. Prefill reads your prompt once. Decode answers word by word, re-reading the model each time. TOPS is horsepower, bandwidth the speed limit: both boxes cruise at two hundred seventy-three gigabytes per second. Decode is city driving. Horsepower wins drag races, and prefill is one. Sipeed's chart: vendor-run, one Qwen model, speculative decoding off, barely ahead. Judge boxes by tokens per second on the Qwen you run, never by TOPS on the tin.

analogy.vehicle: Engine horsepower against the speed limit
analogy.mapping: TOPS is peak horsepower on a bench at ideal RPM; memory bandwidth is the road; decode is city driving where anything past the limit buys nothing, so both boxes cruise at the same 273 GB/s ceiling.
analogy.limit: Horsepower genuinely wins the drag race: at batch prefill, big TOPS do pull ahead, so the number is not useless, just not the one that sets chat speed.
